pull.title: BIP Draft: NestedMuSig2 for BIP340-compatible Signatures
pull.body:
This PR proposes **NestedMuSig2 for BIP340-compatible Signatures**, a BIP draft extending BIP327 MuSig2 to support trees of nested signing groups. Each subgroup participates through its aggregate public key, and the complete tree produces a single BIP340 signature verifiable without knowledge of the internal structure.

The proposal includes the specification, a Python reference implementation, and test vectors covering nested key and nonce aggregation, signing, partial-signature verification, signature aggregation, and error handling. Multi-level examples and randomized tree tests accompany the vectors.

Review is particularly welcome on recursive nonce binding, signer session construction, root tweaks, and compatibility with BIP327 in the flat case. The construction remains n-of-n at each aggregation node.

For every non-root aggregation node at level ''d > 0'', let ''pkd−1 = GetPlainPubkey(keyagg_ctxd)''. In particular, the internal node's ''gacc'' and ''tacc'' values are not inherited by the parent KeyAgg Context. The parent independently derives its own ''gacc'' and ''tacc'' as part of its own BIP327 key-aggregation and tweaking operations. + +Implementations MAY cache intermediate KeyAgg Contexts or other public metadata. Such cached state has no cryptographic role in the parent ''KeyAgg'' invocation beyond the internal aggregate plain public key derived from it. + +====Intermediate Aggregate Public Keys==== + +An intermediate aggregate public key MUST be represented by the 33-byte BIP327 plain-public-key encoding returned by ''GetPlainPubkey''. For an intermediate aggregate point ''Q'', ''GetPlainPubkey'' returns ''cbytes(Q)'', which preserves the parity of ''Q''. The corresponding X-only encoding does not preserve that information and therefore does not uniquely identify the same group element. The recursive key aggregation defined here requires the actual internal aggregate group element as the participant public key at the next aggregation level. + +Intermediate aggregate public keys are independent of a particular signing session and MAY be computed before signing. A participant that knows the corresponding public-key subtree can derive an intermediate aggregate public key locally. A participant that does not know that subtree MAY instead receive the 33-byte aggregate plain public key as the participant key representing the nested subgroup. The recursive signing algorithms do not require disclosure of the subgroup's internal participant keys to parties outside that subgroup. + +====Root Aggregation==== + +The root aggregation node uses the same key-aggregation procedure as every other node. Let ''L0'' be the sorted list of root-level participant plain public keys. The untweaked root KeyAgg Context is ''keyagg_ctx0 = KeyAgg(L0)''. Without aggregate-key tweaks, the root aggregate public key used for BIP340 verification is ''aggpk = GetXonlyPubkey(keyagg_ctx0)''. + +====Aggregate-Key Tweaking==== + +The Nested MuSig2 construction referenced by this specification does not define aggregate-key tweaking. This specification also supports the BIP327 aggregate-key tweaking mechanism only at the root aggregation node. If the application specifies root-level aggregate-key tweaks, it MUST apply them sequentially to ''keyagg_ctx0'' using BIP327 ''ApplyTweak''. Any participants who act as an aggregator at the root level MUST use the same ordered tweak sequence and the same ''is_xonly_t'' value for each tweak. For tweaks ''tweak1, ..., tweakv'', let ''keyagg_ctx0,0 = keyagg_ctx0'' and, for ''i = 1, ..., v'', ''keyagg_ctx0,i = ApplyTweak(keyagg_ctx0,i−1, tweaki, is_xonly_ti)''. Fail if any invocation of ''ApplyTweak'' fails according to BIP327. +

It detects inconsistent session state or an incorrect local signing computation before releasing a partial signature. + +===Partial Signature Verification=== + +''PartialSigVerify'' verifies the second-round contribution by which a participant is represented at a particular aggregation node. The participant may be either an individual leaf signer or a nested aggregation node. + +For an individual leaf signer: +* ''pubnonce'' is the 66-byte public nonce returned by ''NonceGen''; +* ''pk'' is the leaf signer's 33-byte individual plain public key; and +* ''session_ctx'' is the leaf signer's complete Session Context. + +For a nested aggregation node at level ''d > 0'': +* ''pubnonce'' is the node's 66-byte external nonce returned by ''NonceAggExt''; +* ''pk'' is the 33-byte plain aggregate public key ''pkd−1'' by which the node participates at level ''d−1''; and +* ''session_ctx'' is the Session Context truncated to the participant's position at level ''d−1''. + +More precisely, the truncated Session Context contains ''nonce_path = (out0, ..., outd−1)'' and ''cosigner_key_path = (T0, ..., Td−1)'', together with the same root tweak sequence, tweak modes, and message as the complete signing session. In ''Td−1'', the participant occurrence represented by ''pkd−1'' is excluded as required by the Session Context definition. + +Algorithm ''PartialSigVerify(psig, pubnonce, pk, session_ctx)'': +* Inputs: +** ''psig'': the participant's 32-byte partial signature. +** ''pubnonce'': the participant's 66-byte public nonce. For a nested aggregation node, this is its external nonce. +** ''pk'': the participant's 33-byte BIP327 plain public key. +** ''session_ctx'': the Session Context corresponding to the participant's position in the nested signer tree. +* Return failure if ''len(psig) ≠ 32''. +* Return failure if ''len(pubnonce) ≠ 66''. +* Return failure if ''len(pk) ≠ 33''. +* Let ''(Q, gacc, _, b̌, R, _, č) = GetSessionValues(session_ctx, pk)''; return failure if that fails. +* Let ''s = int(psig)''. Return failure if ''s ≥ n''. +* Let ''R*,1 = cpoint(pubnonce[0:33])''; return failure if that fails. +* Let ''R*,2 = cpoint(pubnonce[33:66])''; return failure if that fails. +* Let ''Ř' = R*,1 + b̌⋅R*,2''. +* If ''has_even_y(R)'', let ''Ř = Ř' ''. Otherwise, let ''Ř = −Ř' ''. +* Let ''P = cpoint(pk)''. Return failure if that fails. +* Let ''g = 1'' if ''has_even_y(Q)'', and otherwise let ''g = −1 mod n''. +* Let ''g' = g·gacc mod n''. +* Return success if and only if ''s⋅G = Ř + (č·g' mod n)⋅P''. + +For an individual leaf signer, this equation follows directly from the ''Sign'' algorithm: ''s = k1 + b̌·k2 + č·g·gacc·d' mod n''. For a nested aggregation node, the equation follows recursively. Assume that the required participant contributions at the node satisfy their respective verification equations. Adding those equations combines their nonce terms according to the node's ''NonceAgg'' result and combines their public-key terms according to the node's BIP327 ''KeyAgg'' equation. The node's ''NonceAggExt'' invocation applies the node's intermediate nonce-binding factor to the second aggregate nonce component. Therefore, the scalar sum of the participant partial signatures satisfies the same verification equation under the node's aggregate plain public key and external nonce when evaluated using the Session Context truncated at the node's parent. + +This recursive property lets an aggregate signing node be treated by its parent like a single signing participant. As in BIP327, partial-signature verification exists primarily to identify disruptive participants. A partial signature is not a standalone signature and successful partial-signature verification MUST NOT be interpreted as proof of knowledge or possession of the secret key corresponding to ''pk''. If identifiable aborts are not required, an application MAY omit verification of received partial signatures before aggregation. Implementations SHOULD nevertheless perform the self-verification required by ''Sign'' before releasing locally generated partial signatures. + +===Partial Signature Aggregation=== + +Second-round aggregation proceeds recursively from the leaves toward the root. At a non-root aggregation node, participant partial signatures are combined into one 32-byte partial signature representing that entire nested subgroup at its parent. At the root, the root-level participant contributions are aggregated using the unchanged BIP327 final partial-signature aggregation procedure. + +====Intermediate Partial Signature Aggregation==== + +For a non-root aggregation node, let ''psig1..u'' contain exactly one second-round contribution for every participant occurrence at that node. Intermediate aggregate public keys are not tweaked. Consequently, intermediate aggregation consists only of scalar addition; no tweak contribution is added. + +Algorithm ''PartialSigAggIntermediate(psig1..u)'': +* Inputs: +** The number ''u'' of participant contributions, with ''0 < u < 232''. +** ''psig1..u'': one 32-byte partial signature for every participant occurrence at the aggregation node. +* For ''i = 1, ..., u'': +** If ''len(psigi) ≠ 32'', fail and blame participant occurrence ''i'' for an invalid partial signature. +** Let ''si = int(psigi)''. +** If ''si ≥ n'', fail and blame participant occurrence ''i'' for an invalid partial signature. +* Let ''s = s1 + ... + su mod n''. +* Return ''bytes(32, s)''. + +The returned value is the partial signature that represents the aggregation node to its parent. + +For a node at level ''d > 0'', this aggregate partial signature can be verified with ''PartialSigVerify'' using: +* the external nonce ''NonceAggExt(outd, pkd−1)'' as ''pubnonce''; +* the node's 33-byte aggregate plain public key ''pkd−1'' as ''pk''; and +* the Session Context truncated to levels ''0, ..., d−1''. + +The node's external nonce already incorporates the intermediate nonce-binding factor ''bd''. Transformations introduced by nested descendants are already incorporated into the contributions aggregated in ''outd''. Consequently, the truncated Session Context does not include level ''d'' or any descendant level. An aggregator that wants identifiable aborts SHOULD run ''PartialSigVerify'' on every participant contribution before invoking ''PartialSigAggIntermediate''. ''PartialSigAggIntermediate'' itself validates only the partial-signature scalar encodings and does not establish that the supplied values satisfy their verification equations. + +====Root Partial Signature Aggregation==== + +At the root, each root-level participant is represented by: +* one 33-byte BIP327 plain public key; +* one 66-byte BIP327-compatible participant public nonce; and +* one 32-byte partial signature. + +For a direct leaf participant, these are its individual public key, ''NonceGen'' public nonce, and leaf partial signature. For a nested participant, these are its aggregate plain public key, external nonce, and intermediate aggregate partial signature. Let ''L0'' be the sorted root participant public-key list, and let ''out0'' be the root internal aggregate nonce previously computed from the corresponding root-level participant nonce contributions. Construct the ordinary BIP327 Session Context ''root_session_ctx = (out0, len(L0), L0, v, tweak1..v, is_xonly_t1..v, m)''. The root aggregator MUST supply exactly one 32-byte partial signature for every participant occurrence in ''L0''. Final signature aggregation is performed by invoking the BIP327 algorithm ''PartialSigAgg'' unchanged with the root-level partial signatures and ''root_session_ctx''. + +In particular, BIP327 ''PartialSigAgg'': +* derives the final tweaked root KeyAgg Context; +* derives the root ''MuSig/noncecoef'' binding factor; +* derives the effective root nonce and applies the BIP327 point-at-infinity rule; +* computes the BIP340 challenge; +* sums the root-level partial-signature scalars; +* adds the root tweak contribution ''c·g·tacc mod n'' exactly once; and +* returns the 64-byte signature ''xbytes(R) || bytes(32, s)''. + +No additional NestedMuSig2-specific scalar or tweak term is added during root aggregation. Provided that the root-level contributions are generated from one consistent signing session and all intermediate aggregations follow this specification, the output is an ordinary BIP340 signature under ''GetXonlyPubkey(keyagg_ctxroot)'' for message ''m''. An implementation SHOULD verify the completed signature using ordinary BIP340 verification before releasing or relying on it. + + +==Rationale== + +NestedMuSig2 is based on the recursive construction described in [[https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/223|Nested MuSig2]], but this specification must add concrete conventions that are not fixed by the abstract construction in the paper. In particular, this specification uses BIP327 public-key aggregation, secp256k1 point encodings, BIP340 tagged hashes, BIP327 nonce generation and aggregate-key tweaking, and explicit failure behavior. + +The following subsections explain the principal design choices. + +===Reuse of BIP327 Algorithms=== + +Where the nested construction does not require different behavior, this specification reuses BIP327 algorithms unchanged. + +In particular, the specification reuses BIP327: +* plain-public-key encoding and parsing; +* key sorting and optimized key aggregation; +* leaf nonce generation; +* coordinate-wise nonce aggregation; +* aggregate-key tweaking at the root; and +* final root partial-signature aggregation. + +The intent is to introduce only the operations required for recursive composition. A nested subgroup is reduced to a plain public key, public nonce, and partial signature before it is processed by its parent. At the root, these values therefore have the same external forms as the corresponding values of ordinary BIP327 participants. For a signing tree of depth ''Λ = 1'', no intermediate recursive operation is required. For the same sorted participant-key list, tweak sequence, aggregate nonce, and message, the root key aggregation, root nonce coefficient, effective nonce, challenge, and final partial-signature aggregation therefore use the BIP327 computations. + +===Sorting at Every Aggregation Node=== + +BIP327 ''KeyAgg'' is order-dependent and provides ''KeySort'' for applications that require order-independent aggregation. This specification invokes ''KeySort'' independently at every aggregation node. This provides one canonical BIP327 participant-key ordering for each multiset of participant occurrences and avoids requiring every application to define an additional ordering convention for nested groups. Sorting is local to an aggregation node. An internal node first aggregates using its own sorted participant list, and the resulting aggregate plain public key then appears as one participant key in its parent's sorted list. Duplicate public-key occurrences remain distinct occurrences during this process. + +===Separate Intermediate and Root Nonce Binding=== + +The Nested MuSig2 construction distinguishes intermediate nonce binding from root nonce binding. Intermediate aggregation uses a message-independent binding factor, while the root binding factor additionally commits to the message. + +The nonce-first input order and 32-byte X-only aggregate-key encoding in ''AggNonceCoeffHash'' follow BIP327's [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki#session-context GetSessionValues] computation, ''hashMuSig/noncecoef(aggnonce || xbytes(Q) || m)'', also used by [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327/reference.py the BIP327 reference implementation]. The intermediate computation uses its own tag and omits the message. BIP327 defines the root computation; using this encoding for intermediate binding is a choice of this specification. + +This specification instantiates these roles with separate tagged hashes: +* NestedMuSig/aggnoncecoef for intermediate binding; and +* MuSig/noncecoef for root binding. + +The tags MUST remain distinct. Using a separate intermediate tag separates the two random-oracle roles. Retaining the existing MuSig/noncecoef calculation at the root preserves the BIP327 root computation in the flat ''Λ = 1'' case. Using MuSig/noncecoef at every aggregation level was considered and rejected because the intermediate and root computations serve different roles and have different inputs: intermediate binding is independent of the message, whereas root binding commits to it. + +===Message-Independent Intermediate Aggregation=== + +The message is deliberately omitted from ''NonceAggExt''. This allows nonce aggregation within nested subgroups before the message is determined. Only the root nonce-binding factor and the final BIP340 challenge commit to the message. Including the message in intermediate binding would unnecessarily make every nested subgroup's first-round output message-specific and would remove this preprocessing property without being required by the referenced construction. + +===Retention of Internal Aggregate Nonces=== + +A nested signer requires the internal, pre-binding aggregate nonce of each aggregation node on its path in order to reconstruct the intermediate binding factors during partial signing. An external nonce is insufficient because it already contains the binding transformation applied by ''NonceAggExt''. For this reason, every signing path carries the sequence ''(out0, ..., outΛ−1)''. The specification does not require a particular protocol for transporting these values. Implementations may store them directly or reconstruct them from authenticated or otherwise integrity-protected first-round transcript state. + +===Path-Local Session Context=== + +A leaf signer is not required to know the complete nested signer tree. + +At every aggregation level on its own path, the signer needs: +* the public key by which it is represented at that level; +* the other participant public keys at that level; and +* the internal aggregate nonce for that level. + +These values are sufficient to reconstruct the key-aggregation and nonce-binding coefficients on the signer's path. A subtree that is not expanded on the signer's path can therefore be represented solely by its 33-byte aggregate plain public key. This preserves the abstraction boundary provided by nested aggregation and avoids requiring unrelated participants to learn the internal participant structure of other nested groups. + +===Accumulated Coefficients=== + +A leaf's contribution to the root aggregate key is multiplied by one BIP327 key-aggregation coefficient at every aggregation level on its path. Similarly, its second nonce contribution is transformed by one nonce-binding factor at every relevant level. Consequently, leaf signing uses the accumulated values ''b̌ = b0·...·bΛ−1 mod n'' and ''č = c·a0·...·aΛ−1 mod n''. These products are how the recursive tree collapses into a single root Schnorr verification equation. A nested subgroup has no separate aggregate secret signing key. Instead, its second-round contribution is the scalar sum of its descendants' contributions. + +===Intermediate Partial-Signature Aggregation=== + +Intermediate partial-signature aggregation consists only of scalar addition. No additional tweak term is introduced at a non-root node. Under the restrictions of this specification, intermediate aggregate keys are untweaked, and the required recursive key and nonce coefficients have already been incorporated into the descendants' partial signatures. + +After intermediate aggregation, a nested subgroup is represented at its parent by exactly three protocol objects: +* its 33-byte aggregate plain public key; +* its 66-byte external nonce; and +* its 32-byte aggregate partial signature. + +These objects satisfy the same form of partial-signature verification equation as a direct participant at the parent level. + +===Root-Only Aggregate-Key Tweaking=== + +The referenced Nested MuSig2 construction does not itself specify BIP327 aggregate-key tweaking. This specification permits BIP327 ''ApplyTweak'' only at the root because BIP327 already defines how root tweak parity and the accumulated tweak scalar are incorporated into signing and final signature aggregation. Allowing ''ApplyTweak'' at an intermediate node would introduce additional parity and additive tweak terms into the recursive relation between descendant partial signatures and the public key presented to the parent. The algorithms in this specification do not account for those terms. This BIP therefore does not define intermediate tweaking. This restriction does not imply that an extension supporting such tweaks is impossible; such an extension would require additional algorithms and separate security analysis. + +===Root Signature Aggregation=== + +Final root aggregation uses BIP327 ''PartialSigAgg'' unchanged. + +By the time contributions reach the root, every nested subtree is represented in the same forms expected for an ordinary BIP327 participant. Reusing the BIP327 root algorithm ensures that: +* root aggregate-key tweaks are applied according to BIP327; +* the ordinary MuSig/noncecoef root binding is used; +* BIP327 effective-nonce parity and point-at-infinity rules are retained; +* the root tweak contribution is added exactly once; and +* the final output has the ordinary 64-byte BIP340 signature encoding. + +No NestedMuSig2-specific object is exposed to the final BIP340 verifier. + +==Backward Compatibility== + +NestedMuSig2 does not introduce a new Bitcoin signature type, public-key encoding, transaction witness format, or consensus validation rule. The final output of a successful NestedMuSig2 signing session is an ordinary 64-byte BIP340 Schnorr signature under an ordinary 32-byte BIP340 X-only public key. A BIP340 verifier does not receive, and does not need to know, the nested signer tree, intermediate aggregate keys, internal aggregate nonces, external nonces, or partial signatures. Consequently, software that only verifies the completed BIP340 signature does not require NestedMuSig2 support. + +===Bitcoin Consensus and Taproot=== + +NestedMuSig2 is an off-chain signing protocol. It requires no consensus change, soft fork, or new script opcode. When the resulting X-only aggregate public key is used in a context that already accepts BIP340 signatures, the completed NestedMuSig2 signature is verified using the existing BIP340 verification algorithm. + +In particular, when the root aggregate key is used as a Taproot output key, the blockchain does not reveal whether the signature was produced by: +* a single signer; +* an ordinary BIP327 MuSig2 signing group; or +* a NestedMuSig2 signing tree, + +except to the extent that such information is revealed through other application or transaction metadata. + +This specification does not modify BIP341 Taproot validation rules. + +===Output Script Descriptors=== + +This specification does not define a new output script descriptor expression for representing NestedMuSig2 signer trees. At the time this BIP was written, BIP390 defines the musig() descriptor key expression for BIP327 aggregate keys, but explicitly prohibits nesting one musig() expression inside another. Consequently, a NestedMuSig2 tree cannot be represented directly by nesting the existing BIP390 syntax, for example: musig(KEY_A, musig(KEY_B, KEY_C)) is not a valid BIP390 expression. An existing descriptor may contain the already-computed aggregate public key of a nested subgroup where an ordinary key expression is permitted, but doing so does not encode the subgroup's internal signing structure and is therefore insufficient by itself for wallet recovery or coordination of NestedMuSig2 signing. A descriptor representation for nested signer trees, if desired, requires a separate specification or an extension of the applicable descriptor standard. Such descriptor syntax is outside the scope of this BIP. + +===Wallet and Protocol Compatibility=== + +Wallets, hardware signers, remote signers, and coordinator protocols that understand only BIP327 MUST NOT assume that they can participate internally in a NestedMuSig2 subtree without additional support. + +NestedMuSig2-aware software must additionally understand at least: +* recursive public-key aggregation; +* the distinction between internal and external aggregate nonces; +* ''NonceAggExt''; +* path-local Session Contexts; +* accumulated key and nonce coefficients; and +* intermediate partial-signature aggregation. + +Applications must also coordinate the nested first- and second-round message flow required to move aggregate contributions between child and parent aggregation nodes. No particular wallet, hardware-signing, PSBT, descriptor, or transport protocol integration is defined by this BIP unless explicitly stated elsewhere. + +===ECDSA Compatibility=== + +Like BIP327, NestedMuSig2 produces BIP340 Schnorr signatures and does not produce ECDSA signatures. Existing Bitcoin applications or script contexts that require ECDSA cannot use a NestedMuSig2 signature without separately gaining support for a BIP340-compatible signing context. + +===Version and Protocol Negotiation=== + +The internal NestedMuSig2 signing protocol is not interchangeable with an ordinary BIP327 session of the same participant keys when ''Λ > 1''. In particular, the intermediate tagged hash NestedMuSig/aggnoncecoef, external nonce transformation, path-dependent coefficients, and intermediate partial-signature aggregation are specific to this specification. Applications that exchange NestedMuSig2 protocol messages SHOULD therefore have an unambiguous way to determine that all parties responsible for nested processing are using the same version of this specification. This BIP does not mandate a particular transport-level negotiation mechanism. + +===Nonce Generation=== + +The reference implementation MUST use BIP327 ''NonceGen'' semantics unchanged. + +In particular, leaf nonce generation uses: +* MuSig/aux; and +* MuSig/nonce. + +The reference implementation MUST NOT substitute NestedMuSig2-specific tags for these operations. For deterministic test-vector generation, the implementation MAY expose an internal helper that accepts a caller-supplied 32-byte rand' value. Such a helper exists only to make test vectors reproducible. The ordinary nonce-generation entry point used to model real protocol behavior MUST obtain rand' from a cryptographically secure random number generator as required by BIP327. + +===Intermediate Nonce Binding=== + +The reference implementation of ''NonceAggExt'' and ''GetSessionValues'' MUST compute intermediate binding factors using ''AggNonceCoeffHash'' as defined in [[#external-nonce-aggregation|External Nonce Aggregation]]. + +If either resulting external nonce component is the point at infinity, ''NonceAggExt'' MUST fail rather than serializing the component using ''cbytes_ext''. Every successful ''NonceAggExt'' output therefore consists of two ordinary finite compressed secp256k1 points and can be consumed by the parent's unchanged BIP327 ''NonceAgg'' algorithm. + +===Session and Signing State=== + +The reference Session Context represents ''(nonce_path, cosigner_key_path, tweaks, is_xonly_t, m)''. All Session Context fields are public. Secret nonce state is separate from the Session Context and MUST be treated as single-use. The reference implementation SHOULD model consumption explicitly, for example by using a mutable object whose nonce scalars are erased or marked unavailable when ''Sign'' begins. A call to ''Sign'' MUST consume its supplied secret nonce before performing any subsequent operation that can fail. A second invocation using the same secret-nonce state MUST fail. The reference implementation MAY copy secret-nonce values when required solely for deterministic tests, but such copies MUST be clearly marked as unsafe and MUST NOT be presented as an implementation pattern. + +===Session-Value Computation=== + +''GetSessionValues'' SHOULD expose or make testable the intermediate values required by the NestedMuSig2 test vectors, including: +* reconstructed ''pkd'' values; +* sorted ''Ld'' lists; +* key-aggregation coefficients ''ad''; +* intermediate binding factors ''bd''; +* root binding factor ''b0''; +* final root key ''Q''; +* ''gacc'' and ''tacc''; +* effective nonce ''R''; +* ordinary BIP340 challenge ''c''; +* accumulated binding coefficient ''b̌''; and +* accumulated challenge coefficient ''č''. + +The implementation MUST retain ''c'' and ''č'' as distinct values. The former is required for final root tweak aggregation, while the latter is used for recursive partial signing and partial-signature verification. + +===Partial Signatures=== + +The reference ''Sign'' function returns only the 32-byte partial signature specified by this BIP. ''PartialSigVerify'' accepts one participant public nonce, one participant plain public key, one partial signature, and the Session Context corresponding to that participant's position. This specification does not require a separate nested ''PartialSigVerifyInternal'' API. ''PartialSigAggIntermediate'' implements intermediate subgroup aggregation and performs the scalar aggregation defined above. At the root, the reference implementation MUST use the BIP327 final partial-signature aggregation computation, including the root tweak contribution, without adding any additional NestedMuSig2-specific scalar term. + +===BIP340 Verification=== + +The reference implementation MUST verify every successful end-to-end test vector using ordinary BIP340 verification. The BIP340 verification helper MUST accept messages according to the current BIP340 message semantics and MUST NOT impose a 32-byte-only message restriction. + +Final verification MUST receive only: +* the final 32-byte X-only root public key; +* the message; and +* the final 64-byte signature. + +It MUST NOT depend on any NestedMuSig2-specific signing state. + +===Testing=== + +Running the reference implementation's test suite MUST execute all NestedMuSig2 test-vector suites defined by this specification. Tests that are temporarily disabled during development MUST NOT remain disabled in the version published with the BIP. + +The test suite MUST include checks that: +* unchanged BIP327 primitives continue to satisfy their BIP327 vectors; +* NestedMuSig2-specific vectors produce the expected intermediate values; +* partial signatures verify at both leaf and nested-subgroup boundaries; +* intermediate aggregate contributions verify using truncated Session Contexts; +* secret nonces cannot be reused; +* root aggregation produces the expected signature; and +* every successful final signature passes ordinary BIP340 verification. + +Implementers are encouraged to reproduce the test vectors independently rather than treating the Python implementation as an independent proof of the specification. + +==Security Considerations== + +NestedMuSig2 is an interactive multi-signature protocol. Its security depends on correct nonce handling, correct recursive computation of key and nonce coefficients, consistent session state, and faithful implementation of the algorithms specified in this document. The security considerations of BIP327 apply in addition to the NestedMuSig2-specific considerations described below.

+ +__TOC__ + +==Introduction== + +===Abstract=== + +This document specifies NestedMuSig2, a recursive variant of [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki BIP327] MuSig2 based on the construction introduced by [[https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/223|Nested MuSig2]]. NestedMuSig2 permits a participant at a MuSig2 aggregation node to be represented by the aggregate public key of another MuSig2 signing group, thereby forming a tree of nested signing groups. + +The leaf signers in the tree cooperate to produce a single [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki BIP340]-compatible Schnorr signature under the root aggregate public key. The final signature uses the ordinary 64-byte BIP340 signature encoding and is verified using the ordinary 32-byte BIP340 x-only public-key encoding. Verification requires no knowledge of the internal nesting structure or the leaf signer set. + +===Copyright=== + +This document is licensed under the 3-clause BSD license. + +===Motivation=== + +[https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki BIP327] specifies MuSig2, an ''n''-of-''n'' multi-signature protocol that supports non-interactive public-key aggregation and allows multiple signers to cooperatively produce an ordinary [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki BIP340] Schnorr signature under the resulting aggregate public key. MuSig2 signing consists of two communication rounds; signers first provide public nonces and subsequently provide partial signatures. + +[https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki BIP327] treats the participant public keys as a single, flat key-aggregation set. In some protocols, however, a logical participant may itself be represented by a MuSig2 signing group. Replacing such a group by all of its individual participant keys at the outer aggregation level removes the distinction between the subgroup and the outer signing group. In particular, the subgroup's participant keys become part of the outer key-aggregation set and the outer signing protocol must coordinate with the individual leaf signers rather than with a single aggregate public key representing the subgroup. + +NestedMuSig2 provides recursive composition by allowing a participant public key at one aggregation node to be the child of a Musig2 aggregation node. Repeating this construction forms a tree of signing groups whose root is represented by a single aggregate public key. + +The construction preserves the external BIP340 interface. The completed protocol produces a BIP340 Schnorr signature under the root aggregate public key, and ordinary BIP340 verification does not require knowledge of the underlying signer tree. In particular, a participant represented by an aggregate public key need not reveal to participants outside that subgroup whether that public key represents an individual signer or a further nested MuSig2 group. + +NestedMuSig2 remains an ''n''-of-''n'' construction at each MuSig2 aggregation node. Nesting does not provide ''t''-of-''n'' threshold signing; each MuSig2 node on the signing tree must ultimately include every participant required for the signing session. + +Nested signing retains MuSig2's nonce-contribution and partial-signature stages, while contributions are recursively processed through the aggregation tree. This specification defines the additional key, nonce, session, signing, partial-signature verification, and signature-aggregation rules required to perform that recursive composition while producing a BIP340-compatible final signature. + +==Specification== + +This specification builds directly on [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki BIP327]. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, the notation, secp256k1 constants, point operations, serialization functions, and tagged-hash construction defined in BIP327 apply to this specification. In particular, this specification uses the BIP327 functions ''int(x)'', ''bytes(k, x)'', ''xbytes'', ''cbytes'', ''cbytes_ext'', ''cpoint'', ''cpoint_ext'', and ''has_even_y'', and the tagged hash construction ''hashtag(x)''. + +The following BIP327 algorithms are used unchanged: +* ''IndividualPubkey'' +* ''KeySort'' +* ''KeyAgg'' +* ''KeyAggCoeff'' +* ''GetXonlyPubkey'' +* ''GetPlainPubkey'' +* ''ApplyTweak'' +* ''NonceGen'' +* ''NonceAgg'' + +All input requirements, failure conditions, serialization rules, and blame requirements for those algorithms apply whenever this specification invokes them. + +The [https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki#session-context BIP327 Session Context] and the algorithms ''GetSessionValues'', ''GetSessionKeyAggCoeff'', ''Sign'', ''PartialSigVerify'', ''PartialSigVerifyInternal'', and ''PartialSigAgg'' are replaced by the nested versions specified below. This specification additionally defines ''NonceAggExt'' for converting the internal aggregate nonce of a nested group into the first-round nonce contribution by which that group is represented at its parent aggregation node. This specification reuses only the BIP327 algorithms explicitly identified above. This specification does not specify other BIP327 signing algorithms, including DeterministicSign, for NestedMuSig2 sessions. + +As in BIP327, an algorithm instruction to ''fail'' means the algorithm terminates without producing its normal output. An instruction to ''fail and blame'' a party additionally identifies the party whose invalid protocol contribution caused the failure. This specification does not require a particular API error type or serialization for such failures. + +The [https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/223 Nested MuSig2] paper describes its construction over an abstract prime-order group. This specification instantiates that construction over secp256k1 using BIP327 key aggregation, BIP327's two-nonce representation, and the concrete tagged hashes specified below. This specification defines Bitcoin-specific serialization and aggregate-key tweaking rules that are not part of the abstract construction in the paper. + +===Notation=== + +The following notation is used in addition to the notation of BIP327.
